TCP is a connection-oriented protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery of data through acknowledgments and retransmissions, while UDP is a connectionless protocol that sends datagrams without guarantees, offering lower latency and overhead. In short, TCP prioritizes correctness and flow control, whereas UDP prioritizes speed and simplicity.
